subject: Xenith onboarding: phased integration pace & safeguard matrix
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@xenith.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: jose.ramos@xenith.com, procurement@xenith.com
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI follow-up: detailed phasing, cutover windows, and rollback asks

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the high-level timeline you shared in the RFI. Our procurement and platform teams need a sharper implementation pace and a clear safeguard matrix for internal sign-off. Specifically we need:

- A week-by-week domesticated timeline for integration work (pre-prod + prod cutover).
- Canary / phased rollout windows with criteria for expansion.
- Concrete rollback scenarios and maximum acceptable downtime per service.
- Security/compliance checkpoints (SOC 2 artifact owners, traffic separation, KMS).
- Any exceptions to your standard SLA during canary.

Can you provide a matrix (who does what, acceptance gates, integrations, and estimated resource-days) and an initial Gantt we can drop into our program plan? Our preferred start window is late September; procurement needs a delivery risk rating to justify a two-week procurement approval cycle.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Director, Cloud Programs
Xenith Financial

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@xenith.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, jose.ramos@xenith.com
Date: 2026-08-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: detailed phasing, cutover windows, and rollback asks

Alyssa —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is our proposed Gantt and a Safeguard Matrix (first pass). High level summary below; attachments contain the week-level plan and responsibilities.

High-level phasing (target start: 2026-09-20)
- Week 0 (prep): discovery, credential exchange, KMS setup, pre-prod provisioning.
- Weeks 1-3 (integration): API adapters, auth flows, test harness, basic routing.
- Weeks 4-5 (validation): integration tests, security scans, perf sweeps with 25% synthetic traffic.
- Weeks 6-7 (canary cohort): 2-week canary with 5% traffic then 20% if gate passes.
- Week 8 (ramp): gradual ramp to 50% then full cutover by week 10 assuming all acceptance gates pass.

Canary gates (examples)
- Error rate < 0.5% (5xx + client errors) for 48h
- Latency P95 within agreed SLO +/-15%
- No critical security findings in scan backlog
- Data residency & KMS verification complete

Rollback scenarios
- Fast rollback (0-30 mins): DNS/edge routing redirect to previous model endpoint; affects only new sessions.
- Full rollback (1-4 hours): scale down new pools, restore previous KV cache snapshot, revert routing rules.
- Emergency (4-12 hours): fail open to read-only model endpoint + engage incident runbook.

SLA exceptions during canary
- We propose a temporary SLA carve-out for the first 48 hours of canary limited to latency breaches while we stabilize batching. Any carve-out would be timeboxed and subject to a mitigation credit. Full details in SLA_Exceptions.pdf.

Next steps I propose: internal alignment here at Redwood today, then a 30-minute walkthrough with your engineering + procurement tomorrow. If that works I will send an updated Gantt with explicit resource-day estimates and a risk rating.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Xenith_Migration_Gantt.xlsx (spreadsheet), Safeguard_Matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA_Exceptions.pdf (pdf)

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-03T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick edits to the safeguard matrix (notes)

Vivek / team —

Quick internal notes after skimming the draft:
- Add explicit owner for SOC 2 artifact handoff (we should own evidence generation for model-serving configs).
- Call out network segmentation: Xenith needs a dedicated VPC peering + egress policy; add list of required firewall rules for their infra team.
- Add a data-retention line item: default 30 days for KV cache logs; extendable via contract.
- For canary, recommend starting with a single region (us-east-1) for reduced blast radius.
- Resource-days: integration (APIs + auth) = 10 dev-days, validation = 6 QA-days, canary support = 8 ops-days.

If nobody objects I will fold these into v1.1 and send to Alyssa.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@xenith.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, jose.ramos@xenith.com, procurement@xenith.com
Date: 2026-08-04T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Xenith: updated phased plan, owners, and risk rating (v1.1)

Alyssa / Jose —

Attached is v1.1 with our edits incorporated: explicit SOC 2 evidence owners, recommended single-region canary (us-east-1), network firewall checklist, and resource-day estimates. Summary of changes:

- Owners: Redwood will produce SOC 2 evidence for serving configs and provide the audit trace. Xenith to confirm KMS key admin owners.
- Canary scope: start 5% traffic (48h) -> 20% (72h) -> 50% if gates met.
- Acceptance gates (expanded): automated regression evals on your canonical prompt set, perf tests with live synthetic load, and security scan must be green with <= 5 medium items.
- Risk rating: Moderate (M). Key risks: third-party ETL changes on Xenith side and delayed KMS access. Mitigations listed in matrix.

Procurement note: we can accept a two-week approval window but ask for a signed DocuSign for the canary SLA carve-out so we can schedule capacity. Link to DocuSign provided in related links.

Proposed meeting: 30 minutes tomorrow 10:00 AM PT to run through the matrix and finalize the DocuSign scope.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Safeguard_Matrix_v1.xlsx, Xenith_Migration_Gantt.xlsx

From: Jose Ramos <jose.ramos@xenith.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@xenith.com>, procurement@xenith.com
Date: 2026-08-05T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Xenith: updated phased plan, owners, and risk rating (v1.1)

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for baking in the SOC 2 handoff. Procurement reviewed and we have two asks before we sign:

1) Can you shorten the initial 48h 5% canary to 36h if automated regression passes early? We want faster ramp potential.
2) Please include an explicit runbook step for a KV cache snapshot cadence (we need daily snapshots during canary).

If you can confirm both items we will approve the DocuSign this week and target the Sept 20 start. Also cc'ing procurement — they may request a one-line SLA amendment by EOD.

Best,
Jose Ramos
Senior Program Manager
Xenith Financial
